*Both post-implant monotherapies in the trial achieved non-inferiority compared to dual anti-platelet therapy (DAPT) supporting the potential to simplify post-procedure drug regimens*


MARLBOROUGH, Mass. and SAN DIEGO


, Nov. 2, 2026


/[PRNewswire](http://www.prnewswire.com/) / -- Boston Scientific Corporation (NYSE: BSX) today announced positive six-month primary endpoint results from the SIMPLAAFY randomized controlled trial of the WATCHMAN FLX™ Pro Left Atrial Appendage Closure (LAAC) Device. The study evaluated two single-drug regimens as alternatives to dual anti-platelet therapy (DAPT) following implantation of the device in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF). Key results were presented as a late-breaking clinical trial at Transcatheter Cardiovascular Therapeutics® (TCT®) 2026, the annual scientific symposium of the Cardiovascular Research Foundation® (CRF®) and simultaneously published in[JAMA](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4811682-1&h=3450547893&u=https%3A%2F%2Fjamanetwork.com%2Fjournals%2Fjama%2Ffullarticle%2F10.1001%2Fjama.2026.21361&a=JAMA) .


The WATCHMAN FLX Pro device used in the trial is intended to protect against strokes caused by blood clots that form in the left atrial appendage (LAA) in people with NVAF who need an alternative to long-term blood thinners, and includes HEMOCOAT Technology™, which is designed to enable more controlled, faster healing following implantation. The SIMPLAAFY trial is assessing whether the device, with the addition of HEMOCOAT, may continue to offer similar rates of stroke protection and reduce early bleeding when paired with less-intensive post-implant regimens, and will follow patients through 12 months.


"For patients with NVAF who undergo an LAAC procedure, balancing short-term bleeding risk with the need to maintain stroke protection during post-procedure healing is critical," said Saibal Kar, M.D., study co-chair and director, Structural Heart Disease Interventions and Clinical Research, Los Robles Health System.* "The findings from the SIMPLAAFY trial are encouraging and highlight the potential to meaningfully simplify post-procedure care and reduce medication burden for patients following WATCHMAN FLX Pro implantation."


The study randomized 1,857 patients across 86 clinical study sites in the U.S. to a post-implant regimen of aspirin alone for the duration of the trial or reduced-dose non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulant (NOAC) for the first three months followed by aspirin only or a DAPT regimen of aspirin and clopidogrel antiplatelet medication for the first six months, followed by aspirin only. At six months, data demonstrated that the aspirin alone and reduced-dose NOAC alone regimens each achieved noninferiority to DAPT, with patients on these regimens experiencing less bleeding and equivalent ischemic stroke rates to DAPT (0.7%). Additionally, imaging at 45 days also showed the rate of device-related thrombus, or clotting, was lowest in the patients on a reduced-dose NOAC compared to DAPT (0.9% vs. 3.4%; P=0.01).


"Innovation in LAAC extends beyond device technology to advancing the therapy through improved care delivery and an enhanced experience for physicians and patients," said Brad Sutton, M.D., chief medical officer, Atrial Fibrillation Solutions, Boston Scientific. "The SIMPLAAFY trial provides valuable clinical evidence that can help physicians make more informed decisions about post-implant care and tailor treatment to individual patient needs. Together with advancements like HEMOCOAT Technology, these findings represent meaningful progress toward simplifying treatment and advancing care for patients with atrial fibrillation."


With more than two decades of clinical evidence, the WATCHMAN implant has helped reduce stroke risk for more than 800,000 patients worldwide. The current-generation WATCHMAN FLX Pro device was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in 2023. Enrollment in the Elite AF trial, evaluating the safety and efficacy of the next-generation WATCHMAN Elite™ LAAC Device, commenced in 2026.


For more information about the SIMPLAAFY trial, visit[watchman.com/SIMPLAAFY](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4811682-1&h=3277711615&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.watchman.com%2FSIMPLAAFY&a=watchman.com%2FSIMPLAAFY) .


*Caution: Aspirin alone or reduced dose NOAC alone following LAAC with the WATCHMAN FLX Pro LAAC Device is an investigational post-implant drug regimen.*
